meta.title: 126uW Current-Reuse Telescopic OTA with Class-AB Output Stage -- independent gm/ID redesign (sky130)
meta.source_paper: Shanshan Xie, Hao Chen (UT Austin, 2024/2025 course project) -- "A 126uW Current-Reuse Telescopic OTA with Class-AB Output Stage"
meta.process_note: Original paper: generic 0.18um CMOS, Cadence ADE, 1.8V supply. This redesign: SkyWater sky130 (nfet_01v8/pfet_01v8), gm/ID via the analog-gmid-design skill's real characterized 4D LUT (sky130_nfet_pfet_lut_sample.npz, W_ref=5um) + sizing_recipe.py + stick_diagram.py + ngspice (sky130_fd_pr models, tt corner). Topology and spec targets (Table I, Eq.1-6) are taken from the paper verbatim (independently re-transcribed from the PDF figures before any sizing began); W/L numbers are freshly derived for sky130, not copied from the paper's own 0.18um appendix (used only as an order-of-magnitude plausibility check).

devices.name: M6
devices.role: current-reuse top tail source (gate=Vbias1, fixed) -- shares Vx with M7

devices.name: M7
devices.role: current-reuse top tail source (gate=Vcmfb, CMFB-controlled) -- W(M6):W(M7)=0.7:0.3 heuristic (paper Sec III.C)

devices.name: M1a/M1b
devices.role: input pair, gate=Vip/Vim, source=Vx -- PMOS half of the current-reused gm

devices.name: M2a/M2b
devices.role: telescopic cascode, gate=Vbias2 (fixed) -- boosts output impedance at Vom1/Vop1

devices.name: M3a/M3b
devices.role: telescopic cascode, gate=Vbias3 (fixed)

devices.name: M4a/M4b
devices.role: input pair, gate=Vip/Vim -- SAME gate net as M1a/M1b (this identity IS the current-reuse mechanism: one branch current, two transconductance devices)

devices.name: M5
devices.role: tail current sink (gate=Vbias4), sinks ID(M4a)+ID(M4b)

devices.name: M8/M13, M22/M17
devices.role: Class-AB top current sources (gate=Vbias1), Vom-side/Vop-side resp.

devices.name: M11a/M11b, M20a/M20b
devices.role: diode-connected devices, floating-battery upper leg

devices.name: M9a/M9b, M18a/M18b
devices.role: Monticelli-style floating current source -- adaptive Class-AB bias

devices.name: M12/M10, M21/M19
devices.role: first-stage-output-driven device (gate=Vop1 or Vom1) + fixed-bias tail (gate=Vbias4), modulates the floating battery

devices.name: M14a/M14b, M23a/M24b
devices.role: diode-connected devices, floating-battery lower leg

devices.name: M15/M25
devices.role: big output pull-up, barely-on Class-AB quiescent bias

devices.name: M16/M26
devices.role: big output pull-down, barely-on Class-AB quiescent bias

devices.name: Cc/Rz (x2)
devices.role: Miller compensation + nulling resistor, one per differential output (Vom, Vop)

devices.name: M27-M35
devices.role: biasing/replica-bias generator (Fig.4) -- derives Vbias1-4 from a reference current, replicating Vx/Vy

devices.name: M36a/M36b
devices.role: CMFB output-stage mirror (gate=Vcmfb, feeds M7)

devices.name: M37a/M37b
devices.role: CMFB differential comparator (Voc vs Voc_des)

devices.name: M38
devices.role: CMFB tail

devices.name: M39/M40
devices.role: Voc_des reference generator (long L for process-variation immunity)

devices.name: R1/R2
devices.role: averaging resistors, Vop/Vom -> Voc (CMFB sense)

bill.name: Stage-1 core (M6+M7 tail source = M5 tail sink, BOTH legs already counted)
Stage-2 output, Vom side (M15+M16 barely-on quiescent)
Stage-2 output, Vop side (M25+M26 barely-on quiescent, mirror of Vom side)
Class-AB bias/battery chain, Vom side (M8,M9a/b,M10,M11a/b,M12,M14a/b lumped)
Class-AB bias/battery chain, Vop side (M17,M18a/b,M19,M20a/b,M21,M23a/24b lumped, mirror)

critical_nodes.why: First-stage differential output. M2a/M3a drains land here; Cc/Rz's far end (via the cross-coupled stage-2 input device) also lands here. Sets the dominant pole together with Cc.
critical_nodes.instruction: Route as short, direct, symmetric traces from the row1/row2 stick-diagram stacks to the stage-2 input device (M12/M10 or M21/M19). Length- and shield-match the two traces -- any mismatch shows up directly as input-referred offset.

critical_nodes.why: Vx (M1a/M1b sources, M6/M7 drains) and Vy (M4a/M4b sources, M5 drain) are the buses that make the current-reuse mechanism work -- both M1a(PMOS) and M4a(NMOS) share the SAME Vip gate net. The 6-device series stack (M6-M1a-M2a-M3a-M4a-M5) leaves very little per-device VDS headroom under a 1.8V rail (this report's own VDS budget: 0.30+0.40+0.20+0.20+0.40+0.30=1.80V exactly).
critical_nodes.instruction: Keep Vx and Vy as low-resistance wide-metal buses (they carry the full branch current for both legs) directly over the row3/row4 stacks -- IR drop here directly eats into an already-thin headroom budget.

critical_nodes.why: M15/M25 (PMOS) and M16/M26 (NMOS) drains -- the Class-AB push-pull output, largest device currents in the circuit even at the barely-on quiescent point.
critical_nodes.instruction: Wide, short metal directly from rowP_out/rowN_out to the output pads; size straps for worst-case slewing current (not the quiescent value), since Class-AB's entire point is large instantaneous current. Keep Cc/Rz routing to this net short.

matching_groups.name: row1_pmos_in_casc (M1a,M1b,M2a,M2b)
matching_groups.instruction: Place fingers in exactly this Euler-trail order (build_stick_diagram() output). check_mirror_symmetry() returned False for the raw hierholzer() trail on this row (see section 4) -- for true common-centroid matching, follow up with build_mirror_symmetric_pattern() to force an explicit ABBA-style axis-symmetric order before tapeout; the Euler trail alone only guarantees a single continuous diffusion, not axis symmetry.

matching_groups.name: row2_nmos_in_casc (M3a,M3b,M4a,M4b)
matching_groups.instruction: Same treatment as row1; this row's Euler trail IS verified mirror-symmetric (check_mirror_symmetry()==True). Sits physically below row1 with Vy as the shared bottom bus.

matching_groups.name: rowP_out (M15,M25) / rowN_out (M16,M26)
matching_groups.instruction: Both rows verified mirror-symmetric and closed-circuit Euler trails (0 odd-degree nodes) with box-shape PASS (ratio 1.00, 68 fingers each row). M16/M26's row sequence: M26 -> M26 -> M16 -> M16 -> M26 -> M26 -> M16 -> M16 ...

power_branches.name: M15/M25, M16/M26 (Class-AB output)
power_branches.instruction: Sized for gm2=3mS at the paper's own nominal design current (ID=88.2uA/device design point per this report's STEP1); actual barely-on quiescent is ~11.0uA/device (STEP2, same W, reverse-LUT bias point). Strap for worst-case slewing current, not the quiescent value -- consult sky130 EM rules for actual strap width.

compensation.name: Cc/Rz (x2, Vom and Vop paths)
compensation.instruction: Cc=500fF is fixed by the paper's own Eq.4 beta derivation (Cf=Cs=500fF) -- keep routing parasitic to/from Cc well under ~25fF (5% of Cc) or re-run the stage-2 gm2 derivation with the updated Cc. Rz (nulling resistor, standard form R~=1/gm(M16-type)) was not independently re-derived in this pass -- confirm the RHP-zero cancellation condition with SPICE before tapeout.

stacks: row1_pmos_in_casc + row2_nmos_in_casc (stage-1 signal core, 2-row box, ratio 1.00)
stack_placement.instruction: 3 separate physical cells. find_hub_merge_candidates() (run over the FULL device list, before any stack split, per SKILL.md sec6/design-report-spec.md sec1.6) flagged (pmos,VDD):4 and (pmos,Vx):2 as merge candidates -- decision: do NOT merge row3(M6/M7, finger_w~1.18um) with rowP_out(M15/M25, finger_w~5.88um); finger widths differ 5x between the bias-current row and the large-signal output row, so forcing one diffusion row would blow the box-shape ratio and physically couple a low-swing bias net to the output's large-signal swing.

layout_guide.biasgen_cmfb_note: M27-M40 (Fig.4 biasing generator, Fig.5 CMFB) were sized (section 3) but not run through the stick-diagram pipeline in this pass -- they are low-current (1-2uA range) reference/replica-bias branches, not matching- or bandwidth-critical, and are lower priority for finger-level layout care than the 3 cells above. Honest scope note.
out_of_scope: Exact ESD/guard-ring rules, foundry DRC (spacing/enclosure/antenna) -- run the sky130 DRC deck.
Rz's exact value/derivation -- not independently re-derived from Eq.1-6 in this pass; confirm with SPICE.
Fig.4/Fig.5 (biasing, CMFB) finger-level stick diagrams -- sized but not layout-analyzed (see note above).

Full nonlinear transient/slew-rate/noise/CMRR/PSRR verification -- this report's SPICE covers single-device .op cross-checks and a bottom-up DC power budget, not the paper's full settling-time/noise/CMRR/PSRR simulation suite.

M9a/M9b/M11/M12/M14 (Class-AB floating-battery internal topology, Fig.3) -- connectivity beyond the top-level current source/battery/output roles was not resolved to gate-level certainty from the scanned schematic resolution; sized by functional-role current allocation (SKILL.md sec1.5), not by a fully confirmed node-by-node netlist. Flagged, not silently assumed.

floorplan.scope_note: pack_floorplan_grouped() output, real run -- 3 cells covered by this pass (core_signal_cell/bias_tail_cell/stage2_output_cell). M27-M40 (biasing generator, Fig.4) and CMFB (Fig.5, M36-M40/R1-R2) were sized but not run through the stick-diagram/floorplan pipeline in this pass -- see the honest scope note in section 7 (layout guide). This is a partial-scope floorplan, not a full-circuit one.
